question: A team judges its Claude-assisted research notes purely by whether colleagues say they enjoy reading them. What is the greatest risk in using this as the measure?
options: A) Positive ratings may encourage the team to produce more notes than colleagues have time to read.
B) Fluent, confident notes can be well liked while carrying errors nobody checked against sources.
C) Colleagues who read quickly may rate the notes higher than colleagues who read them thoroughly.
D) Preferences drift over time, which makes this quarter's ratings hard to compare with last quarter's.
correct_answers: B) Fluent, confident notes can be well liked while carrying errors nobody checked against sources.
explanations: Producing more notes is a workload effect rather than a risk to the reliability of the notes.
Correct. Reader satisfaction measures how the notes read, not whether they are right, so a confident and wrong note scores as well as a correct one and the error is adopted.
Variation between readers adds noise to the measure, but the deeper problem is what it measures at all.
Drift makes comparison harder over time; it does not explain why accuracy goes unmeasured.
